'''''Setaria verticillata''''' is a species of [[Poaceae|grass]] known by the common names '''hooked bristlegrass''',<ref>{{PLANTS|id=SEVE3|taxon=Setaria verticillata|access-date=11 November 2015}}</ref> '''rough bristle-grass'''<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |access-date=2014-10-17 }}</ref> and '''bristly foxtail'''. It is native to Europe, but it is known on most continents as an [[introduced species]] and often a [[noxious weed]]. It is a hardy [[bunchgrass]] which grows in many types of urban, cultivated, and disturbed habitat. It is a weed of many types of [[agriculture|agricultural crops]], growing in [[vineyard]]s and fields. Herbicide-resistant strains have been noted.<ref name=issg>{{Cite web |url=http://www.issg.org/database/species/ecology.asp?si=927&fr=1&sts=&%20ang=EN&ver=print&prtflag=false |title=ISSG Database |access-date=2010-07-28 |archive-date=2016-03-04 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304060549/http://www.issg.org/database/species/ecology.asp?si=927&fr=1&sts=&%20ang=EN&ver=print&prtflag=false |url-status=dead }}</ref>

This is an annual grass with decumbent or erect stems growing up to a meter long. The leaf blades are up to 25 centimeters long and have a long sheath around the stem. The [[inflorescence]] is a dense [[panicle]] up to 15 centimeters long which tapers at both ends. It contains many small spikelets and bristles. The bristles have tiny backwards-pointing barbs that help them hook onto clothing or animal fur, facilitating their [[biological dispersal|dispersal]].<ref name=issg/>

Seeds of the grass are used to make [[beer]] in South Africa and [[porridge]] in Namibia.<ref name=issg/> They have been used as a [[famine food]] in India.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.hort.purdue.edu/newcrop/faminefoods/ff_families/poaceae.html |title=Purdue: Famine Foods |access-date=2010-07-28 |archive-date=2007-02-06 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070206031104/http://www.hort.purdue.edu/newcrop/FamineFoods/ff_families/POACEAE.html |url-status=dead }}</ref>
